One picture of where everything sits, then the three paths a request can take. Every scenario
follows one of those paths, so the table at the end names the path for each, and each scenario's
page says what happens along it. **Solid** parts are built and running; **dashed** parts are
planned, labelled with the phase that brings them. A built part that a later phase changes stays
solid, and its label adds the change with that phase. [The plan](design/plan.md) holds the reasons.

```{mermaid}
  orca -- starts --> claude_mac

  webapp -- "HTTPS over Tailscale" --> tss

  pi_mac -- "SSH tunnel, make tunnel" --> swap

  owui -.-> front
  agent_tmux -.-> front
  front -. "internal key" .-> swap
  front -. "asks before a load" .-> gate
  gate -. "loads, unloads" .-> swap
  gate -. "reads and lifts its hold" .-> brake

```

- **Everything on the Spark listens on 127.0.0.1**, except SSH and `tailscale serve`'s port 443.
  The tailnet's rules let my own devices reach the Spark on those two ports only, and ufw allows
  SSH alone from the LAN.
- **Three accounts on the Spark.** Mine, the admin; `spark`, which runs llama-swap, the engines and
  the brake; and `agent`, for coding agents in tmux, with no sudo, no docker and keys of its own.
  Root runs the web services from its own copies of their units. From Phase 2a, `spark` also runs
  the gate, beside the brake, and two system users of their own run the front (`spark-front`) and
  the model downloads (`spark-pull`).
- **From Phase 2a (planned), the front takes 127.0.0.1:9100** with the same keys, so pi, the web UI
  and `agent` change nothing. systemd holds 9100 and the gate's two sockets, so they are never free,
  even while the front or the gate restarts, or crashes again and again. llama-swap moves to 127.0.0.1:900 and the engines to
  800 and up, below 1024, where no other user can listen, and only the internal keys reach
  llama-swap. The gate decides every load, unloads idle models and lifts the brake's hold; the
  brake stays a unit of its own, so it runs even while the gate is down, and then sends its own
  alert. The web containers drop their capabilities, so they can't take those ports either. ntfy
  on the Synology
  carries notifications to my phone, over the tailnet or the home LAN only, and to my Mac from
  Phase 2b. [The plan](design/plan.md#the-front-and-the-gate-phase-2a) says why.
- **Claude never uses the Spark's models.** Claude Code and Claude Desktop talk straight to
  Anthropic, wherever they run; Orca only starts them. The Spark is a separate mode.

## Reaching the Spark

```{mermaid}
flowchart LR
  classDef planned stroke-dasharray: 5 5

  piT["pi on the Mac<br/>in a terminal or Orca"]
  ui["web UI<br/>on the Mac or the phone"]
  piA["pi as agent<br/>in tmux on the Spark"]
  cc["Claude Code<br/>anywhere"]
  app["an app with its own key<br/>Phase 3"]:::planned
  fam["family and friends<br/>over a shared Tailscale node · Phase 6"]:::planned
  guest["a guest at an event<br/>venue LAN, a key each · Phase 6"]:::planned

  tunnel["SSH tunnel<br/>over Tailscale, or the LAN alias"]
  guestui["guest web UI<br/>events only · Phase 6"]:::planned
  serve["tailscale serve, 443<br/>Tailscale only"]
  owui["Open WebUI"]
  searx["SearXNG"]
  front["the front, 127.0.0.1:9100 · Phase 2a<br/>the same keys, then an internal key"]:::planned
  swap["llama-swap, 127.0.0.1:9100<br/>a key on every request<br/>to 127.0.0.1:900 · Phase 2a"]
  litellm["LiteLLM on a LAN port · Phase 3<br/>ahead of the front, in its place, or not at all"]:::planned
  anthropic(("Anthropic"))

  piT --> tunnel --> swap
  ui --> serve --> owui --> swap
  owui --> searx
  piA --> swap
  cc --> anthropic
  tunnel -.-> front
  owui -.-> front
  piA -.-> front
  front -.-> swap
  app -.-> litellm
  litellm -. "through the front or in its place, if Phase 3 adds it" .-> swap
  fam -.-> serve
  fam -.-> litellm
  guest -.-> guestui -.-> litellm
  guest -.-> litellm
```

pi on the Mac reaches llama-swap only while `make tunnel` runs, since nothing on the Spark listens
beyond 127.0.0.1 but SSH. The web UI needs Tailscale: on another tailnet, over WireGuard, the LAN
alias still carries SSH and so pi's tunnel, but the web UI waits. `agent`'s pi needs no tunnel. From
Phase 2a (planned), the same tunnel, address and keys reach the front instead, which checks the key
and forwards to llama-swap on its new port with a key of its own; no client changes. Only the
inference routes go through: llama-swap's admin routes stay out of every client's reach. From Phase
3, apps reach the models with a key of their own; Phase 3 decides whether LiteLLM sits ahead of the
front, takes its place, or isn't used at all, the front growing what Phase 3 needs. From Phase 6,
family and friends reach the web UI and LiteLLM over a shared Tailscale node that shows them only
the Spark, and guests at an event reach LiteLLM and a guest web UI of their own, on the venue's
network only.

## Loading a model

```{mermaid}
flowchart TD
  classDef planned stroke-dasharray: 5 5

  req["a request names a model"] --> loaded{"already loaded?"}
  loaded -- yes --> answer["the engine answers"]
  loaded -- no --> launch["llama-swap starts it<br/>through spark launch<br/>Phase 2a: only with the gate's ticket"]
  launch --> held{"is the brake holding<br/>new loads?"}
  held -- yes --> refuse["refused, with its reason<br/>make status shows it"]
  held -- no --> fits{"does its footprint fit in<br/>free memory, less the reserve?"}
  fits -- no --> refuse
  fits -- yes --> load["the engine loads"] --> answer
  low["free memory falls<br/>toward the freeze band"] --> brake["the brake warns, then holds new loads<br/>and unloads models, on-demand ones first<br/>Phase 2a: idle ones first, and on the rate of fall"]
  brake --> held

  front["Phase 2a: the front, on 9100, checks the key and the route<br/>and counts the requests in flight"]:::planned
  gdown["gate down: loaded models keep serving,<br/>new loads refused with gate_down, a 503;<br/>at boot, nothing loads"]:::planned
  ask{"the gate: brake clear, and the footprint fits what's free for a load:<br/>available memory less the reserve, the growth the loaded models are owed,<br/>any load starting and any make-room hold that isn't mine?<br/>one load at a time, my keys first"}:::planned
  gload["the gate gives spark launch a ticket and loads it through llama-swap;<br/>spark launch keeps the hold check and a zero-wait fit check"]:::planned
  hold["the gate keeps the request waiting<br/>for its key's wait: 30 s for mine, 10 minutes for agent's"]:::planned
  inline["refused inline, like any API error: a 409, which clients don't retry,<br/>memory needed against what's free for a load, the top holders, one next step and a code"]:::planned
  release["Phase 2a: the gate lifts the hold after 5 minutes above 28 GiB, if the reloads fit,<br/>once an hour at most; a hold found at boot waits for me"]:::planned
  idle["Phase 2a: the gate also unloads on-demand models idle for 60 minutes<br/>and runs make-room, which holds the room for me;<br/>both drain the model first, so neither cuts off a request in flight"]:::planned

  req -.-> front
  front -. loaded .-> answer
  front -. "not loaded" .-> ask
  front -. "gate down" .-> gdown
  ask -. yes .-> gload
  gload -.-> answer
  gload -. "load fails" .-> inline
  ask -. no .-> hold
  hold -. "fits in time" .-> gload
  hold -. "time is up" .-> inline
  brake -.-> release
  ask -.- idle
```

A model loads only if it fits: nothing is evicted to make room, and nothing is swapped for a
smaller model. Free memory is the smaller of `MemAvailable` and what the GPU can allocate, and the
reserve stays free, because overcommitting a GB10 can freeze it without an out-of-memory kill.

From Phase 2a (planned, dashed), a request reaches the front first. A model that's loaded is
forwarded at once; for one that isn't, the front asks the gate, which admits one load at a time,
my keys ahead of `agent`'s. What's *free for a load* is then available memory less the reserve,
the growth the loaded models are still owed, and any room make-room is holding for me, which my
own requests may load into and `agent`'s may not. If the model doesn't fit, the request waits
for its key's wait, then gets a refusal that says why, in the client itself. `spark launch` starts
nothing without the gate's ticket, and keeps today's checks as backstops that never wait. The
reserve stays 24 GiB: the design lowered it to 22, and it went back to 24 the same day.

## Apps and speech (Phase 3, planned)

```{mermaid}
flowchart LR
  classDef planned stroke-dasharray: 5 5

  app["an app or pipeline<br/>with its own key"]:::planned --> litellm["LiteLLM: limits and a wait per key,<br/>refusals inline, the real model named"]:::planned
  litellm -.-> pg[("Postgres<br/>keys and usage")]:::planned
  litellm -. "through the front or in its place, if Phase 3 adds it" .-> swap["llama-swap"]
  swap --> chat["chat and embeddings"]
  swap --> stt["whisper, interactive"]
  swap -.-> batch["whisper, batch"]:::planned
  swap -.-> diar["speaker labels"]:::planned
```

Today the web UI and pi reach llama-swap directly with llama-swap's own keys. From Phase 2a they
reach the front instead, with the same keys, and it already waits per key and refuses inline. From
Phase 3, my own pipelines and homelab apps come in through LiteLLM, each with a key of its own; it
never logs what they send. Phase 3 decides whether LiteLLM sits ahead of the front, takes its
place, or isn't used at all, the front growing what Phase 3 needs.

([S23](scenarios/s23-upgrade-day.md); [Updates](how-to/updates.md)).
